questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — tenant-search-indexer (multi-tenant search, Next.js + Drizzle + PostgreSQL). Verified finding T3: `startTenantRebuild()` sets `rebuildingGeneration` and only `completeTenantRebuild()` clears it, so when a rebuild job throws, the job is marked FAILED but the flag stays set and every later `requestIndexRebuild()` answers 409 'A rebuild is already in progress' until someone runs manual SQL. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: a REBUILD job that throws must leave the tenant able to request a new rebuild; the failure path releases `rebuildingGeneration` instead of leaving it for manual SQL.

[w3] Release the flag conditionally: only for a failed REBUILD job, and only while `rebuildingGeneration` still equals that job's generation (a new repository function whose WHERE carries the generation), never a blind reset in the runner's generic catch.
[w2] Scope includes cleaning up the failed generation's partially written documents with the existing tenant-scoped `deleteGenerationDocuments()`, so the next rebuild does not inherit them.

[w2] Allowed files: src/services/indexingJobRunner.ts, src/repositories/tenantSearchStateRepository.ts and one new test file under tests/ (the vitest config sets no include, so the default *.test.ts pattern picks it up).
[w3] Boundary: the 409 guard in `requestIndexRebuild()` stays exactly as it is, no schema or migration change, no automatic re-queue of FAILED jobs, and findings T1/T4/T6 are out of scope.
[w2] Test command: `npm test` (vitest run) with the repositories and the db client mocked through vi.mock, the way the existing tenant-isolation test does it, so no PostgreSQL is needed.

[w2] Stop condition: a test where the rebuild snapshot throws shows the job marked FAILED and the flag released for that generation, plus a test that a failed INCREMENTAL job leaves the flag alone; the concurrent-request race is reported, not fixed.
keyPoints.quote: concurrent rebuild requests can both succeed

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What are the likeliest ways an agent goes wrong on this task, and what in your brief prevents each?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It deletes or softens the 409 check so a stale flag is simply ignored, which reopens double rebuilds instead of fixing the failure path.

[w3] It clears the flag in the shared catch for every failed job; incremental jobs fail routinely (T2), so an incremental failure would wipe the marker of a rebuild that is still queued and let a second rebuild for the same generation be requested.
keyPoints.quote: a ticket changed twice between runs wedges incremental indexing for its tenant

keyPoints.text: [w2] It resets the flag but leaves the half-written next-generation documents behind, because the snapshot upserts run outside any transaction.
[w2] It adds a retry loop or re-queues FAILED rebuild jobs, a new feature the brief did not ask for.
keyPoints.quote: `FAILED` is terminal and nothing re-queues it

keyPoints.text: [w1] It wraps the whole rebuild (snapshot reads and upserts) in one long transaction to make it 'atomic', changing the cutover design that deliberately keeps only the flip and the old-generation delete together.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent says the stuck-rebuild fix is in and tests pass. What do you check before you accept it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] The new failure test is red on the original runner (the flag is still set after the throw) and green on the fix; ask for both runs.
[w3] `requestIndexRebuild()` is untouched in the diff and still throws ConflictError while a rebuild is genuinely in progress.
[w2] The release is keyed on the generation, so a late failure from an old job cannot clear the marker of a newer rebuild; a test or the WHERE clause shows it.
[w2] src/db/schema.ts is unchanged and no drizzle migration appears in the diff.
[w1] The handback flags that tenants already stuck stay stuck until a one-off data repair, since the fix only changes future failures.
